Title: Turn a long email thread into an open-issues list
Prompt: Using the emails I referenced, build an open-issues list for [matter]. Table columns: # | Issue | Raised by (name and party) | Who owes the next action | What is owed | Due date (write 'none stated' if no date) | Status (open, agreed, closed) | Date of the latest email on it. Treat an issue as closed only if every side confirmed it in writing. List items with no clear owner in a separate section. Do not guess dates or owners.
HowToUse: Open Copilot Chat, type / and use the Emails tab to add the most recent messages in the thread, then paste the prompt.
WatchOuts: Check each item against the cited emails before you circulate the list, and keep it marked draft until an attorney has reviewed it.

Title: Summarize an email thread: decided, open, next
Prompt: Summarize this email thread in 3 bullets: what was decided, what's still open, and what I need to do next.
HowToUse: In Outlook, open the conversation and select Summary by Copilot, or paste this into Copilot Chat with the thread attached.
WatchOuts: Click the numbered citations to jump to the original emails before you act on the summary.

Title: Polite decline with two alternative times
Prompt: Write a polite email declining a meeting invitation for [day], offering two alternative times later in the week.
HowToUse: In Outlook, start a reply, select the Copilot icon, then Draft. Adjust length or tone, select Keep it, then edit and send.
WatchOuts: Check the times against your calendar before sending.

Title: Summarize a document and pull out deadlines and dollar amounts
Prompt: Summarize this document in 5 bullet points, then list any deadlines, dollar amounts or action items it mentions, with the section or page where each appears.
HowToUse: In Copilot Chat, select + (Add content) and attach the file, or type / and start typing the file name.
WatchOuts: Long documents can be summarized unevenly. Spot-check the figures against the source pages.

Title: Compare a term sheet to the draft loan agreement
Prompt: Compare the attached term sheet with the attached draft loan agreement. Build a table: Term | Term sheet says | Loan agreement says (with section number) | Consistent? (yes, no, not addressed) | Note. Cover at least: loan amount, interest rate and index, maturity and extensions, amortization, prepayment, yield maintenance or exit fee, recourse and carve-outs, reserves, financial covenants (DSCR, LTV, debt yield), cash management, guarantor requirements and assignment. Then list anything in the term sheet that the draft does not reflect. Quote section numbers. If something is unclear, say so rather than inferring.
HowToUse: Attach both documents in Copilot Chat. For long agreements, run it on the economic terms first, then the covenants.
WatchOuts: This is an issue-spotting aid, not a sign-off. Confirm every 'not addressed' row yourself.

Title: Extract key loan terms into a deal summary table
Prompt: From the attached loan agreement, fill in this table: Borrower | Guarantor(s) | Lender | Loan amount | Closing date | Maturity date | Extension options | Interest rate (index and spread, or fixed) | Prepayment terms | Recourse and carve-outs | Reserves (type and amount) | Financial covenants. Give the section number for every value. Write 'not found' rather than guessing.
HowToUse: Attach the agreement in Copilot Chat. Paste the result into your deal summary template and check each cell.
WatchOuts: Defined terms can hide the real number (for example 'Applicable Margin'). Follow the definition.

Title: Build a closing checklist from a commitment letter
Prompt: Using the attached commitment letter, draft a closing checklist for [deal name]. Group items under: Loan documents, Borrower and guarantor organizational documents, Title and survey, Third-party reports, Insurance, Opinions, Closing deliverables and Post-closing. Columns: # | Item | Responsible party (if stated) | Source (section of the commitment) | Status (leave blank). Only include items the commitment actually requires, and list anything ambiguous separately at the end.
HowToUse: Attach the commitment letter. Paste the table into your firm checklist template and add firm-standard items.
WatchOuts: Copilot only sees the commitment you gave it. Add lender-specific and program requirements yourself.

Title: Review a title commitment: requirements and exceptions
Prompt: Review the attached title commitment. List every Schedule B-I requirement and Schedule B-II exception in a table: # | Item (short description) | Type (requirement or exception) | Recorded document reference, if any | What it appears to affect | Suggested next step (satisfy at closing, request removal, endorsement, request copy, or attorney to review) | Question for the title company. Do not draw conclusions about insurability.
HowToUse: Attach the commitment PDF in Copilot Chat.
WatchOuts: Scanned PDFs may read poorly. If items are missing, check the page count against the original.

Title: Summarize a redline by who it favors
Prompt: Summarize the changes in this redline. Table: Section | What changed | Favors lender, borrower or neutral | Substantive or clean-up. Put substantive changes first. Quote the changed language for anything substantive.
HowToUse: Open the comparison document in Word and use Copilot, or attach it in Copilot Chat.
WatchOuts: Copilot reads the document as it appears. Confirm it picked up deletions as well as insertions.

Title: Check defined terms
Prompt: List every defined term in this document with the section where it is defined. Then flag: terms used but never defined, terms defined but never used, terms defined more than once, and capitalized words that look like defined terms but are not defined.
HowToUse: Open the document in Word and select Copilot.
WatchOuts: Terms defined in another document (for example the loan agreement) will show as undefined. That's expected.

Title: Check cross-references
Prompt: Check the internal cross-references in this document. List any reference to a section, exhibit or schedule that does not exist, and any reference whose target section seems to be about a different topic than the sentence implies. Give the location of each.
HowToUse: Open the document in Word and select Copilot.
WatchOuts: Run it after the last round of renumbering.

Title: Proofread without changing substance
Prompt: Proofread this section for typos, inconsistent capitalization of defined terms, and number and word mismatches (for example 'ten (11)'). Don't change the substance. List each fix as: location | current text | suggested text.
HowToUse: Select the section in Word, then ask Copilot.
WatchOuts: Accept fixes yourself rather than letting Copilot rewrite the section.

Title: Explain a provision in plain English
Prompt: Explain [provision, for example the cash management provisions in Section X] in plain English for a business reader, in under 120 words. Describe what it does and when it applies. Do not give legal conclusions.
HowToUse: Attach or open the document, then ask.
WatchOuts: Review before it goes to a client. It is a starting draft, not advice.

Title: Track diligence received and outstanding from email
Prompt: Search my emails from the last [2 weeks] about [deal name]. List the diligence items that were received and those still outstanding. Table: Item | Received or outstanding | From whom | Date of the email | Link to the email. If an item is mentioned but it's unclear whether it arrived, list it as 'unclear'.
HowToUse: Open Copilot Chat (work mode) and paste the prompt with the deal name filled in.
WatchOuts: Copilot only finds what's in your mailbox. Items sent to a colleague won't appear.

Title: Brief me before a call
Prompt: I have a call about [matter] at [time]. From my recent emails, chats, meetings and files about it, give me a one-page briefing: where things stand, open issues, what the other side last asked for, and three questions I should raise. Cite your sources.
HowToUse: Open Copilot Chat in Teams or on the web 10 minutes before the call.
WatchOuts: Open the cited emails for anything you plan to rely on during the call.

Title: Recap a Teams meeting
Prompt: Recap this meeting: decisions made, action items with owner and due date, and open questions. Keep it under 200 words and note anything that was discussed but not decided.
HowToUse: Open the meeting in Teams (it must have been recorded or transcribed) and select Copilot or Recap.
WatchOuts: Only works for meetings with transcription on. Confirm owners and dates with the attendees.

Title: Draft a weekly client status update
Prompt: Draft a short status update to [client contact] on [deal]: what got done this week, what's outstanding and who owes it, and the target closing date. Plain, professional tone, under 150 words. Use only facts from my recent emails about this deal, and leave a [bracket] wherever you're not sure.
HowToUse: Use Draft with Copilot in Outlook, or Copilot Chat in work mode so it can read your recent emails.
WatchOuts: Check every date and every name before it goes to the client.

Title: A second opinion on a tricky email
Prompt:
Review my draft reply below. Tell me how it may come across to [recipient], flag anything that's ambiguous or could be read as a commitment, and suggest a clearer version that keeps my voice.

[paste draft]
HowToUse: In Outlook, use Coaching by Copilot on your draft, or paste the draft into Copilot Chat with this prompt.
WatchOuts: You decide what to change. Copilot doesn't know the history with this person.

Title: Rent roll quick analysis
Prompt: In this rent roll, show total occupied square feet, occupancy percentage, and leases expiring within 24 months of [date], grouped by year. Flag rows with missing rent, square footage or expiration dates.
HowToUse: Open the rent roll in Excel. Format the data as a table (Ctrl+T) first, then select Copilot.
WatchOuts: Copilot in Excel works best on clean tables with one header row. Check totals against the source.

Title: Compare a tenant estoppel to the lease
Prompt: Compare the attached tenant estoppel certificate to the attached lease (and amendments). Table: Topic | Estoppel says | Lease says (with section) | Consistent? Cover: parties, premises, term and commencement date, current rent, rent escalations, security deposit, options (renewal, expansion, purchase, termination), defaults claimed and prepaid rent. List any inconsistencies first.
HowToUse: Attach the estoppel, the lease and every amendment.
WatchOuts: If an amendment is missing, Copilot will flag a false inconsistency. Check the lease chain first.

Title: Find precedent documents
Prompt: Find documents in our SharePoint and OneDrive about [topic, for example a bridge loan with a mezzanine intercreditor] from [timeframe]. List file name, location, last modified date and a one-line description of each. Don't open or summarize them yet.
HowToUse: Open Copilot Chat in work mode.
WatchOuts: Copilot only finds files you already have access to.

Title: Draft time-entry narratives from my day
Prompt: From my sent emails, meetings and documents I edited on [date], draft time-entry narratives grouped by client and matter: Matter | Task description (start with an active verb, client-billing style) | Time estimate from meeting length, where there was a meeting. Mark every estimate clearly as an estimate. Don't invent tasks.
HowToUse: Open Copilot Chat in work mode at the end of the day.
WatchOuts: A drafting aid only. You confirm every entry and every time value before entering it.

Title: Plan my week
Prompt: Look at my calendar and flagged emails for next week. List deadlines and meetings by day, point out conflicts, and suggest two-hour focus blocks for drafting.
HowToUse: Open Copilot Chat in work mode on Friday afternoon or Monday morning.
WatchOuts: Copilot suggests blocks but won't book them. Add them yourself.

Title: Have Copilot write the prompt for you
Prompt: I want to [describe the task]. Before you do anything, ask me up to five questions you need answered to do it well. Then write the best prompt for this task that I can save and reuse.
HowToUse: Use it whenever you're not sure how to ask. Save the result to the Prompt Library.
WatchOuts: None. It's a good habit.

Title: Estate plan document request list
Prompt: Draft a client-friendly checklist of the documents and information we need for an estate plan review for [client type, for example a married couple with a closely held business]. Group by category, with one sentence on why we need each item. Keep it to one page.
HowToUse: Paste the result into the firm letterhead template and edit.
WatchOuts: Compare it to the firm's standard intake list before sending.
